CABINET

 13 NOVEMBER 2026

 REPORT OF THE PORTFOLIO HOLDER FOR
 HOUSING AND PLANNING

A.3 ANNUAL HOUSING IMPROVEMENT, PERFORMANCE & ASSURANCE REPORT
 2025/26

PART 1 – KEY INFORMATION

PURPOSE OF THE REPORT

To present the first Annual Housing Improvement, Performance & Assurance Report 2025/26
for consideration and endorsement; to provide consolidated assurance on performance,
improvement, risk and compliance with the Consumer Standards; and to establish a developing
annual reporting approach supported by an accessible public-facing snapshot.


EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report presents the first Annual Housing Improvement, Performance & Assurance Report
2025/26 (Appendix A). Cabinet has received a number of reports on housing matters during the
year; this report brings that evidence and hard data together into a single, consolidated
assessment of performance, improvement, risk and regulatory assurance.

Tenant Satisfaction Measures provide the golden thread through the report, connecting tenants’
experience with operational performance, complaints, service improvement, governance and
the evidence required by the Regulator of Social Housing. The report is therefore intended to
serve three connected audiences: tenants, who require clear and accessible information with
which to scrutinise their landlord; Cabinet, which requires consolidated evidence to support
oversight, challenge and decision-making; and the Regulator of Social Housing, which requires
robust evidence of compliance with the Consumer Standards.

Significant progress has been made during the year to strengthen governance, assurance and
regulatory compliance through completion of the Consumer Standards self-assessment,
implementation of the Housing Improvement and Delivery Plan, enhanced performance
monitoring arrangements and increased opportunities for tenant scrutiny and influence.

The report highlights positive progress in areas including tenant engagement, governance,
assurance, tenancy sustainment, workforce development and understanding diverse tenant
needs.

It also identifies areas requiring continued improvement, including repairs satisfaction,
complaint handling, data quality, implementati

[page 2]
Standards. It is deliberately balanced, presenting both positive progress and areas of weakness
or risk, while recognising that this first report is a work in progress and will evolve as data quality,
benchmarking and reporting arrangements mature.

The priorities identified for 2026/27 focus on strengthening data quality and assurance
arrangements, improving customer satisfaction, implementing key transformation programmes,
embedding workforce changes and continuing delivery of the Housing Improvement and
Delivery Plan. The additional capacity arising from the recently approved Housing Service
restructure will support stronger performance management, service improvement and delivery
of these priorities as posts are implemented.


RECOMMENDATION(S)

It is recommended that Cabinet:

1) notes the contents of the Annual Housing Improvement, Performance & Assurance
 Report 2025/26, being the first report of this type for Tendring District Council,
 attached as Appendix A and recognises that the reporting framework will continue to
 evolve as data quality, benchmarking and assurance arrangements mature;

2) acknowledges the overall assurance position set out within the report; and

3) supports the continued delivery of the Housing Improvement and Delivery Plan and
 associated improvement priorities identified for 2026/27.



REASON(S) FOR THE RECOMMENDATION(S)

The recommendations ensure that Cabinet receives evidence-based assurance regarding
housing service performance, improvement activity and regulatory readiness, while supporting
continued oversight of the Housing Improvement and Delivery Plan and compliance with the
Consumer Standards. They also recognise that this is the first consolidated annual report and
that its presentation will evolve over time.

The detailed report balances the volume of evidence required for effective governance and
regulatory assurance with the need for accessible communication. The delegated public-facing
snapshot will provide a proportionate account for tenants and the wider public, presenting both
good performance and areas of concern without obscuring the underlying evidence.

  Maintaining and improving council housing.
  Delivering high-quality services for residents.

In addition, the report supports compliance with the Regulator of Social Housing Consumer

Report to: Cabinet
 26 November 2026


 Q2 BUDGET MONITORING AND MEDIUM TERM FINANCIAL STRATEGY UPDATE –
 GENERAL FUND & HOUSING REVENUE ACCOUNT 2026/27


Report by: Leader of the Council, Cabinet Member for Finance & Strategy

Supported by: Assistant Director of Finance & Governance

Enquiries to: Andrew Wilks, Finance Manager (Management Accounting),
 andrew.wilks@basildon.gov.uk

 Enclosure No. 2 – Capital & Investment Strategy Q2 Report

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

This report presents the forecast outturn for 2026/27, at the end of September 2026 (Quarter
2).

The overall summary position for the General Fund is a projected overspend of £3.8m. This
projected overspend has increased by £0.4m since Quarter 1. One of the key contributing
factors continues to be temporary accommodation to cover our statutory duty around
homelessness and more specifically the availability of alternative accommodation to reduce
the need to use expensive nightly paid accommodation. There are other cost pressures
related to capital financing, staffing and risk of savings non-delivery. These are partly offset
by additional planning income.

The overall summary position for the Housing Revenue Account (HRA) is a projected
overspend of £3.2m. This is an improvement of £1.3m since Quarter 1. This continues to
be due to the significant rise in repair costs, dealing with damp and mould cases, as well as
additional costs associated with delivering against the requirements of the Regulatory
Notice issued by the Regulator for Social Housing.

The full financial position is summarised within the report, with specific focus and detail on
the key contributing factors and the actions being taken to mitigate against them. To the
extent that any pressures are unable to be managed by the end of the financial year, the
Council will need to apply revenue reserves to balance the budget. The detailed breakdown
of all services can be found in Enclosure No. 1.

The information contained within this report is a key input to

[page 2]
enabling appropriate mitigating actions to be considered as future budgets are developed
and set.

The report also includes an update on the Council's Capital Programme and Treasury
Management position as at Quarter 2, providing Members with assurance regarding the
delivery of capital projects, the management of borrowing and investments, and compliance
with the approved Treasury Management Strategy.

Members are asked to review the report and provide observations on the projected outturn
position, including any significant variances and their implications for the delivery of key
service objectives within the Council's Corporate Plan. The revenue position was presented
to the Finance, Procurement and Efficiency Scrutiny Committee on 16 November 2026 and
the Capital & Investment Strategy Quarter 2 Report was considered by the Audit & Risk
Committee on 4 November 2026.

BACKGROUND

Budget monitoring is a vital component of the Council’s financial management framework,
supporting effective decision making, informing the year end closure process and
contributing to the ongoing development of the Medium Term Financial Strategy (MTFS). It
plays a key role in maintaining strong financial governance and ensuring the Council’s long-
term financial sustainability.

The timely identification of budget variances, emerging pressures and financial risks
enables appropriate corrective action and mitigating measures to be implemented, helping
to safeguard the delivery essential services and support the achievement of the Council’s
Corporate Plan objectives.

In addition, a number of the variances identified through budget monitoring are expected to
have ongoing financial implications beyond the current year. As a result, these issues will
inform future budget setting decisions and contribute to the development of the MTFS.

mitigate these as far as possible before the end of the financial year. A formal recovery plan
process has been introduced whereby services need to set out the actions being taken each
month to improve the financial position. The improvement in the financial position since
Quarter 1 demonstrates early signs of this having a tangible impact. Services are expected
to manage minor variances within existing resources at directorate level. Any implications
will be reported to Members as appropriate, and any overspend remaining at the year-end
will need to be met from reserves.

Please note that the monitoring position of the capital programme is reported separately
through the Capital & Investment Strategy quarterly reports presented to Audit & Risk
Committee. These have been consolidated into this report on the revenue budget position

1.1 To provide Members of the Committee with an updated Quarter 2 (Q2) financial

 into the future.

LONG LEASE AGREEMENT: FORESHORES AT RIVER BLACKWATER AND DOWNS
ROAD BOATYARD

1. PURPOSE OF THE REPORT

1.1 To request agreement for a renewal lease of 25 years for the foreshore abutting
 Downs Recreation Ground at River Blackwater.

1.2 To request agreement for a renewal lease of 25 years for the foreshore adjoining
 Downs Road Boatyard to bring both leases in line with each other.


2. RECOMMENDATION

 That the Council agrees a renewal lease for 25 years for the foreshore abutting
 Downs Recreation Ground at River Blackwater and the foreshore at Downs Road
 Boatyard allowing both leases to expire in 2051.


3. SUMMARY OF KEY ISSUES

3.1 The current tenant is a long-standing tenant of Maldon District Council. The
 leaseholder runs a business from the adjoining boatyard using both leased
 foreshores as necessary access points.

3.2 The current tenant has held a lease for the abutting Downs Recreation Ground at
 River Blackwater (see APPENDIX 1 – image A) with Maldon District Council since
 1993. The lease was initially granted for a period of seven years and then extended
 to 25 years.

3.3 The tenant has leased the foreshore area adjoining Downs Road Boatyard
 (APPENDIX 1 - image B) since 2008 under a separate 20-year lease. As this lease
 is nearing the end of its term, approval is sought to extend the lease period to align
 them.

3.4 The lease for the foreshore adjoining Downs Road Boatyard has expired; however,
 the tenant remains in lawful occupation under the security of tenure provisions of the
 Landlord and Tenant Act 1954. This enables the tenant to continue occupying the
 premises on the existing lease terms while a renewal lease is negotiated and
 completed.

3.5 As the security of tenure provisions of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954 were not
 excluded from either lease, the current tenant, has statutory rights to seek a renewal
 tenancy. In practice, this means that the Council is required to grant a new lease on
 broadly similar terms, unless there are statutory grounds for opposing renewal.


 Our Vision: Where Quality of Life Matte

[page 2]
3.6 The Council is therefore working with the tenant to agree new lease terms for both
 the foreshore abutting Downs Recreation Ground on the River Blackwater and the
 foreshore adjoining Downs Road Boatyard. As the additional foreshore lease was
 granted in 2008 for a term of 20 years, it is proposed that the renewal arrangements
 align the terms of both leases.


4. CONCLUSION

4.1 The current tenant has a legal right a new lease on similar terms for the foreshore
 abutting Downs Recreation Ground at River Blackwater and foreshore adjoining
 Downs Road Boatyard under the provisions of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954.
 The proposed 25-year lease will meet our legal obligations and ensure stability for
 the business.


5. IMPACT ON PRIORITIES AS SET OUT IN THE CORPORATE PLAN 2025 - 2028

5.1 Growing our economy

5.1.1 The agreement of a new lease and lease extension will provide stability for the long
 running business, allowing continued investment in the skills and facilities required to
 contribute to Maldon’s maritime heritage.


6. IMPLICATIONS

 (i) Impact on Customers – None.

 (ii) Impact on Equalities – None.

 (iii) Impact on Risk (including Fraud implications) – If Members do not
 approve the proposed lease renewal, the tenant has the right to seek renewal
 of the tenancy by applying to Court. The Court will likely grant a new lease
 and will set the terms, rent etc over which the Council will have less control.

 (iv) Impact on Resources (financial) – There will be no impact on the Council’s
 Finances, as a result of agreeing these lease extensions.

 (v) Impact on Resources (human) – The legal work will be carried out in house.

 (vi) Impact on Devolution / Local Government Reorganisation – None
 currently.

ASSET DISPOSAL POLICY

1. PURPOSE OF THE REPORT

1.1 To consider and approve the Council’s Asset Disposal Policy, attached at
 APPENDIX 1 to this report.


2. RECOMMENDATION

 That the Council’s Asset Disposal Policy attached at APPENDIX 1 to this report be
 approved.


3. SUMMARY OF KEY ISSUES

3.1 The Assets Disposal Policy, attached at APPENDIX 1, establishes a consistent and
 transparent framework for assessing and progressing the disposal of Council-owned
 land and property.

3.2 The Policy identifies three principal disposal routes: open market disposal, disposal
 to special purchasers and Community Asset Transfer. Proposals will be assessed
 against the Council’s operational and strategic requirements, supported by
 appropriate valuation, legal and financial advice. Community Asset Transfer
 applicants will need to demonstrate measurable public benefit, community support,
 financial sustainability and suitable governance, operational and management
 capacity.

3.3 The Policy sets out a staged process covering initial assessment, due diligence,
 options appraisal, independent valuation, engagement, approval and legal
 completion, together with post-completion monitoring and updates to Council
 records.

3.4 Decisions remain subject to the Constitution and Scheme of Delegation. Any decision
 for a large site disposal either by sale or lease will still require Council approval. This
 policy ensures a consistent approach to all requests and ensures Officers have a
 clear policy to follow when making delegated decisions for disposals currently set out
 within the constitution.

3.5 Appropriate safeguards, including restrictive covenants, overage, clawback and
 reversionary provisions, will be considered to protect the Council’s interests where
 appropriate.

3.6 Applicants or purchasers will normally meet the Council’s legal and reasonable
 professional costs unless otherwise agreed in writing.


 Our Vision: Where Quality of Life Matters

[page 2]
3.7 Disposals will not normally be progressed where an asset remains required for
 Council purposes, a substantially similar request has been determined within the
 preceding six months, or an application fails to meet the relevant criteria.

4. CONCLUSION

4.1 Approval of the Assets Disposal Policy will provide a clear governance process for
 the public and officers dealing with requests to purchase Council assets,

5. IMPACT ON PRIORITIES AS SET OUT IN THE CORPORATE PLAN 2025 - 2028

5.1 Delivering Good Quality Services

5.1.1 Having a clear policy will allow the Council to provide clear guidance and
 transparency regarding the management of Council assets. This will allow officers to
 provide a clear process and criteria for assessment of disposal requests.

6. IMPLICATIONS

 (i) Impact on Customers – There are no direct impact on customers arising
 from the recommendations in this report.

 (ii) Impact on Equalities – There are no direct equality implications arising from
 the recommendations in this report.

 (iii) Impact on Risk (including fraud implications) – The Policy ensures that all
 decisions are made in a clear and consistent matter reducing the risk of
 challenge.

 (iv) Impact on Resources (financial) – There are no direct financial implications
 arising from approval of the Policy. Any decisions made will have an impact
 on Council finances, but these will be advised in any future disposal reports.

 (v) Impact on Resources (human) – None.

 (vi) Impact on Devolution / Local Government Reorganisation – There are no
 direct implications arising from the recommendations in this report.
